epic_title: Check-In Configuration — Temperature, Early Check In & Confirmation

stories.title: Temperature Acknowledgement Toggle with Conditional Input
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to enable a Temperature Acknowledgement setting via a toggle and provide a custom prompt so that drivers are asked to confirm their temperature reading during check-in.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Admin IMS User is on the Check-In Settings page
acceptance_criteria.when: When they toggle Temperature Acknowledgement ON
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a text input for the temperature prompt appears below the toggle with a default placeholder value

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Temperature Acknowledgement toggle is ON
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin enters a custom prompt and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the setting is persisted and the custom prompt is returned on subsequent page loads

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Temperature Acknowledgement toggle is OFF
acceptance_criteria.when: When the settings page renders
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the temperature prompt input is hidden and the setting is excluded from the active check-in configuration

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a screen reader user navigates the Temperature Acknowledgement section
acceptance_criteria.when: When focus reaches the toggle
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the toggle has an accessible label, the conditional input is announced when revealed, and the expanded/collapsed state is conveyed via aria-expanded

stories.reasoning: Temperature acknowledgement is a configurable check-in step. The conditional reveal pattern keeps the UI clean when the feature is disabled and requires aria-expanded for accessibility.

stories.title: Temperature Validation — Invalid Format and Required Value
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to see clear validation errors when the temperature prompt is empty or in an invalid format so that I cannot save a misconfigured setting.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Temperature Acknowledgement toggle is ON and the prompt input is empty
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin attempts to save
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an inline error 'A value is required' is displayed below the input and focus moves to the invalid field

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the admin enters a value containing unsupported characters or exceeding the max length
acceptance_criteria.when: When the input loses focus or the admin attempts to save
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an inline error 'Invalid format' is displayed below the input

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a validation error is displayed
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin corrects the input and re-triggers validation
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the error message is removed and the save action is enabled

stories.reasoning: Validation prevents saving incomplete or malformed temperature settings. Inline errors with focus management follow WCAG error identification guidelines.

stories.title: Early Check In Toggle with Hours and Instruction Inputs
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to enable Early Check In via a toggle and configure the allowed hours and driver instructions so that drivers can check in ahead of their scheduled time within controlled limits.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Admin IMS User is on the Check-In Settings page
acceptance_criteria.when: When they toggle Early Check In ON
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a numeric input for 'Hours before scheduled time' and a text area for 'Driver instructions' appear below the toggle

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Early Check In toggle is ON
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin enters valid hours and instructions and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: Then both values are persisted and returned on subsequent page loads

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Early Check In toggle is OFF
acceptance_criteria.when: When the settings page renders
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the hours and instruction inputs are hidden and the early check-in setting is excluded from the active configuration

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a screen reader user navigates the Early Check In section
acceptance_criteria.when: When focus reaches the toggle and it is switched ON
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the toggle has an accessible label, aria-expanded reflects the state, and the revealed inputs are announced with their labels and any default values

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the Early Check In toggle is turned ON, WHEN the instruction field is displayed, THEN it is pre-populated with default text: 'Due to earlier arrival time, you cannot check in via regular process. Please contact Facility Administrator directly via phone number {TRAFFIC_CLERK_PHONE}'.
stories.reasoning: Early Check In requires two conditional inputs (numeric hours + text instructions) making it the most complex toggle section. The 5-point estimate reflects the additional input handling and default text logic.

stories.title: Early Check In Validation — Numbers Only, Required Value, Default Text
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want validation on the Early Check In fields so that only valid numeric hours and non-empty instructions can be saved.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Early Check In toggle is ON and the hours input contains non-numeric characters
acceptance_criteria.when: When the input loses focus or the admin attempts to save
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an inline error 'Numbers only' is displayed below the hours input

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Early Check In toggle is ON and the hours input is empty
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin attempts to save
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an inline error 'A value is required' is displayed below the hours input and focus moves to the invalid field

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Early Check In toggle is ON and the instructions text area is cleared
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin attempts to save
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an inline error 'A value is required' is displayed below the instructions field

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the admin has not modified the instructions text area
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin saves with the default text still present
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the default text is accepted as a valid value and the setting saves successfully

stories.reasoning: Validation ensures hours are numeric and both fields are non-empty. Accepting the default instruction text as valid avoids forcing unnecessary edits.

stories.title: Confirmation Step Toggle with Customizable Success Text
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to enable a Confirmation Step via a toggle and customise the success message so that drivers see a branded completion screen after check-in.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Admin IMS User is on the Check-In Settings page
acceptance_criteria.when: When they toggle Confirmation Step ON
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a text area for the success message appears below the toggle with a default success message pre-populated

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Confirmation Step toggle is ON
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin edits the success text and saves
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the custom success text is persisted and returned on subsequent page loads

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Confirmation Step toggle is OFF
acceptance_criteria.when: When a driver completes check-in
acceptance_criteria.then: Then no confirmation screen is shown and the check-in flow ends at the last active step

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a screen reader user navigates the Confirmation Step section
acceptance_criteria.when: When focus reaches the toggle
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the toggle has an accessible label, aria-expanded conveys the state, and the success text area is announced with its label when revealed

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the Confirmation Step toggle is ON, WHEN the confirmation text field is displayed, THEN it contains the default value: 'Driver Check In is successfully completed! Please wait for the call from Traffic Clerk for Dock assignment and further instructions'.
stories.reasoning: The confirmation step provides closure to the driver check-in flow. Customisable text allows each facility to brand the experience. Follows the same conditional-reveal pattern as other toggle settings.

epic_title: QR Code Generation, PDF Export & Print

stories.title: QR Code Setting Toggle and Generate Button
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to enable QR Code generation via a toggle and click a Generate button so that a unique QR code is created for my facility's driver check-in.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the Admin IMS User is on the Check-In Settings page
acceptance_criteria.when: When they toggle QR Code ON
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a 'Generate QR Code' button appears below the toggle

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR Code toggle is ON
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin clicks the Generate button
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a request is sent to the QR generation backend and a loading indicator is shown on the button until the response returns

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR Code toggle is OFF
acceptance_criteria.when: When the settings page renders
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the Generate button is hidden and no QR code is associated with the active configuration

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the screen is rendered, WHEN navigated via keyboard, THEN all interactive elements are focusable with visible focus indicators per WCAG 2.1 AA.
stories.reasoning: The toggle and Generate button are the admin-facing entry point for QR code creation. Depends on the backend service (US-027) to produce the QR image.

stories.title: QR Code Modal with Org-Specific Title and QR Image
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to see the generated QR code in a modal dialog with my organisation's name so that I can preview and share the code before printing.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR code has been generated successfully
acceptance_criteria.when: When the response returns
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a modal opens displaying the QR code image and the organisation name as the modal title

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR Code modal is open
acceptance_criteria.when: When the user presses the Escape key or clicks the close button
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the modal closes and focus returns to the Generate button

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR Code modal is open
acceptance_criteria.when: When the user presses Tab repeatedly
acceptance_criteria.then: Then focus is trapped within the modal and cycles through the interactive elements (close button, Save as PDF, Print) without escaping to the background

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a screen reader user opens the QR Code modal
acceptance_criteria.when: When the modal renders
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the modal has role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-labelledby pointing to the org title, and the QR image has descriptive alt text

stories.reasoning: The modal provides a preview context for the QR code. Focus trap and Escape-to-close are essential WCAG 2.1 AA requirements for dialog components.

stories.title: QR Code Generation Backend Service
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want the system to generate a unique QR code for my facility so that drivers can scan it to begin the check-in process.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given an authenticated admin sends a POST request to the QR generation endpoint with a facility ID
acceptance_criteria.when: When the server processes the request
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a QR code image is generated encoding the facility-specific check-in URL and the image is stored and its URL returned in the response

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a QR code already exists for the facility
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin requests generation again
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the previous QR code is invalidated and a new one is generated with a fresh URL token

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR generation request is missing required fields or the user is unauthorised
acceptance_criteria.when: When the server validates the request
acceptance_criteria.then: Then it returns a 400 or 401 status with a descriptive error message and no QR code is created

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the screen is rendered, WHEN navigated via keyboard, THEN all interactive elements are focusable with visible focus indicators per WCAG 2.1 AA.
stories.reasoning: The backend service is the foundation for QR code functionality. Regeneration invalidates old codes to prevent stale links. This must be built before the frontend Generate button can function.

stories.title: Save as PDF Download and Print Dialog
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to save the QR code as a PDF or print it directly from the modal so that I can post the code at my facility for drivers to scan.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR Code modal is open
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin clicks 'Save as PDF'
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a PDF file containing the QR code image and organisation name is generated and downloaded to the user's device

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the QR Code modal is open
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin clicks 'Print'
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the browser's native print dialog opens with the QR code and organisation name formatted for printing

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the PDF generation fails due to a client-side error
acceptance_criteria.when: When the download does not start within 5 seconds
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an error toast is displayed informing the admin to retry

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the screen is rendered, WHEN navigated via keyboard, THEN all interactive elements are focusable with visible focus indicators per WCAG 2.1 AA.
stories.reasoning: PDF and Print are the two distribution methods for QR codes. Both actions originate from the modal, so this story depends on the modal being built first.

epic_title: Mobile API, Security & Accessibility Audit, Error Handling & Audit Logging

stories.title: Mobile Read-Only Settings API Endpoint
stories.user_story: As a Standard IMS User (mobile driver), I want the mobile app to retrieve the current check-in settings for my facility so that I see only the steps that the admin has enabled.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a driver's mobile app sends a GET request to the settings endpoint with a valid facility ID
acceptance_criteria.when: When the server processes the request
acceptance_criteria.then: Then it returns a JSON payload containing only the enabled check-in settings with their configured values

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the mobile app requests settings
acceptance_criteria.when: When the response is returned
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the endpoint is read-only and does not accept PUT, POST, or DELETE methods, returning 405 Method Not Allowed for those verbs

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the facility ID is invalid or the request is unauthenticated
acceptance_criteria.when: When the server validates the request
acceptance_criteria.then: Then it returns a 404 or 401 status respectively with a descriptive error message

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the screen is rendered, WHEN navigated via keyboard, THEN all interactive elements are focusable with visible focus indicators per WCAG 2.1 AA.
stories.reasoning: The mobile API is the bridge between admin configuration and the driver experience. Read-only enforcement prevents mobile clients from modifying settings.

stories.title: Toggle OFF on Admin Excludes Setting from Mobile Response
stories.user_story: As a Standard IMS User (mobile driver), I want disabled settings to be absent from the mobile API response so that I am not shown check-in steps that are turned off.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given an admin has toggled Temperature Acknowledgement OFF
acceptance_criteria.when: When the mobile app requests the settings endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the temperature_acknowledgement key is absent from the JSON response

acceptance_criteria.given: Given an admin has toggled Early Check In OFF
acceptance_criteria.when: When the mobile app requests the settings endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the early_check_in key is absent from the JSON response

acceptance_criteria.given: Given all toggles are OFF for a facility
acceptance_criteria.when: When the mobile app requests the settings endpoint
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the response returns an empty settings object with a 200 status and the mobile app displays the default check-in flow

acceptance_criteria: GIVEN the screen is rendered, WHEN navigated via keyboard, THEN all interactive elements are focusable with visible focus indicators per WCAG 2.1 AA.
stories.reasoning: Excluding disabled settings from the response simplifies mobile client logic — the app renders exactly what is present without needing to check enabled flags.

stories.title: SAST and Dependency Security Scan — Zero Critical/High
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want the platform to pass static application security testing and dependency vulnerability scans with zero critical or high findings so that the system meets organisational security standards.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the CI/CD pipeline runs on a pull request or merge to main
acceptance_criteria.when: When the SAST scan completes
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the build fails if any critical or high severity findings are detected and the findings are reported in the pipeline output

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the dependency scan runs against the project's lock file
acceptance_criteria.when: When vulnerabilities are evaluated
acceptance_criteria.then: Then all direct and transitive dependencies are scanned and the build fails if any critical or high CVEs are found

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a scan produces medium or low findings
acceptance_criteria.when: When the pipeline completes
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the build passes with warnings and the findings are logged for review in the next sprint

stories.reasoning: Security scanning in CI ensures vulnerabilities are caught before deployment. Zero critical/high is the minimum bar for production readiness.

stories.title: WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility Audit on All Pages
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want all pages to pass a WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit so that the platform is usable by people with disabilities and meets compliance requirements.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given an automated accessibility scanner (e.g., axe-core) runs against every page
acceptance_criteria.when: When the scan completes
acceptance_criteria.then: Then zero critical or serious violations are reported for WCAG 2.1 AA success criteria

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a manual keyboard navigation test is performed on each page
acceptance_criteria.when: When the tester tabs through all interactive elements
acceptance_criteria.then: Then every element is reachable, has a visible focus indicator, and the tab order matches the visual layout

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a screen reader test is performed on each page
acceptance_criteria.when: When the tester navigates using landmarks and headings
acceptance_criteria.then: Then all content is announced correctly, form inputs have associated labels, and dynamic content changes are conveyed via aria-live regions

acceptance_criteria.given: Given colour contrast is evaluated across all pages
acceptance_criteria.when: When text and interactive elements are measured
acceptance_criteria.then: Then all text meets a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text against their backgrounds

stories.reasoning: A dedicated accessibility audit catches issues that per-story a11y ACs may miss. Combining automated and manual testing provides comprehensive coverage.

stories.title: API Failure Handling with Error Toast and Retry
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want to see a clear error notification when an API call fails and have the option to retry so that I can recover from transient errors without losing my work.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given an API call fails with a 5xx server error or network timeout
acceptance_criteria.when: When the error response is received
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an error toast appears with a user-friendly message and a 'Retry' button, and the toast is announced to screen readers via aria-live='assertive'

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the error toast is displayed with a Retry button
acceptance_criteria.when: When the admin clicks Retry
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the original API request is re-sent and the toast is dismissed if the retry succeeds

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the retry also fails
acceptance_criteria.when: When the second failure response is received
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the error toast updates to suggest contacting support and the Retry button remains available

stories.reasoning: Graceful error handling with retry prevents data loss and reduces support tickets. The toast pattern provides non-blocking feedback that does not disrupt the admin's workflow.

stories.title: Audit Logging for All Setting Changes
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want all check-in setting changes to be recorded in an audit log so that there is a traceable history of who changed what and when.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given an admin saves a change to any check-in setting
acceptance_criteria.when: When the server persists the change
acceptance_criteria.then: Then an audit log entry is created containing the user ID, timestamp, setting name, previous value, and new value

acceptance_criteria.given: Given an admin toggles a setting ON or OFF
acceptance_criteria.when: When the toggle change is saved
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the audit log records the toggle state change with the setting identifier and the old and new boolean values

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the audit log is queried
acceptance_criteria.when: When results are returned
acceptance_criteria.then: Then entries are ordered by timestamp descending and include all fields needed for compliance review

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the audit log write fails
acceptance_criteria.when: When the logging service is unavailable
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the setting change still succeeds but an alert is raised to the operations team for the missed audit entry

stories.reasoning: Audit logging is essential for compliance and troubleshooting. Recording previous and new values enables diff-based review. Decoupling audit writes from the save path prevents logging failures from blocking admin operations.

stories.title: Optimistic Locking for Concurrent Edits
stories.user_story: As an Admin IMS User, I want the system to prevent my changes from silently overwriting another admin's concurrent edits so that no configuration changes are lost.

acceptance_criteria.given: Given two admins load the same settings page simultaneously
acceptance_criteria.when: When the first admin saves a change and the second admin then attempts to save
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the second admin receives a 409 Conflict response because the version has changed since their page load

acceptance_criteria.given: Given a 409 Conflict response is received
acceptance_criteria.when: When the UI processes the error
acceptance_criteria.then: Then a notification informs the admin that the settings were modified by another user and prompts them to reload before retrying

acceptance_criteria.given: Given the admin reloads the settings after a conflict
acceptance_criteria.when: When the page refreshes
acceptance_criteria.then: Then the latest saved values are displayed and the version token is updated so the next save attempt can succeed

stories.reasoning: Optimistic locking via a version field prevents last-write-wins data loss when multiple admins edit settings concurrently. The 409 + reload pattern is a standard approach that avoids complex real-time locking.
